responsibilities.Capability: Decide what problem is worth solving, whose problem it is, and what success should mean.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: AI may generate formulations; a human/institution must own the adopted objective.

responsibilities.Capability: Identify moral conflicts, consent, rights, authority, distribution, and recourse.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Capability cannot by itself settle legitimacy.

responsibilities.Capability: Decide what evidence is sufficient, what remains uncertain, and when to suspend judgment.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: AI can estimate; the learner must understand how confidence was earned.

responsibilities.Capability: Retain enough internal knowledge to notice category errors, impossible claims, broken units, causal confusion, or evaluator gaming.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Near-ASI may exceed manual verification; the goal becomes detecting classes of failure and knowing when independent experts/institutions are needed.

responsibilities.Capability: Select among abundant plausible outputs; articulate why one is more fitting, coherent, elegant, humane, robust, or original.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Taste is not 'AI cannot do this'; it is formation of human preference and quality judgment under abundance.

responsibilities.Capability: Listen, negotiate, teach, lead, collaborate, repair conflict, and build trust.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: These remain normative and relational even when AI mediates them.

responsibilities.Capability: Observe, measure, build, repair, move, care, and notice physical constraints.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Prevents an entirely synthetic epistemic life.

responsibilities.Capability: Set permissions, decompose tasks, create evals, monitor drift, preserve provenance, and revoke authority.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: This becomes a universal literacy, not an AI-specialist elective.

responsibilities.Capability: Create organizations and rules that can learn, dissent, stop work, audit power, and survive leader/model error.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Individual judgment is insufficient under superhuman systems.

responsibilities.Capability: Choose commitments, preserve plural traditions, create culture, and decide what forms of life are worth sustaining.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Do not reduce education to labor-market complementarity.

responsibilities.Capability: Maintain fallback skills, redundancy, privacy, security, and reversible choices under uncertain capability transitions.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: Avoid brittle dependence on one model/provider/institution.

responsibilities.Capability: Evaluate long-horizon effects on children, institutions, environment, culture, and future option value.
responsibilities.AGI/ASI interpretation: High capability increases the stakes of objective and governance mistakes.
